description: Terse, technical backend engineer working on a payments/ledger service. Talks in decisions, requirements, and postmortems. Low-affect, high-density.

messages.text: We decided to use PostgreSQL 16 with Drizzle as the ORM for the payments service.
Decision: all internal service-to-service calls go through the gRPC gateway, no direct HTTP.
We're using Redis for idempotency keys on the checkout endpoint.
Requirement: every migration must be reversible and tested on a staging snapshot first.
We can't use MongoDB for the ledger table, compliance requires ACID transactions.
Actually, the retry backoff base is 250ms, not 500ms like I said earlier.
The correct value for the connection pool size is 20, I misquoted 10 in standup.
We tried doing idempotency with a unique constraint alone but it didn't work under concurrent retries.
Failed approach: in-memory rate limiting, it doesn't survive a pod restart.
Check the schema at src/db/schema.ts for the ledger table shape.
See https://github.com/acme/ledger-service/blob/main/docs/reconciliation.md for the reconciliation job — I keep calling it 'the reconciliation doc' in standup, same thing.
I always prefer explicit transaction boundaries over relying on ORM auto-commit.
Never use SELECT * in the reporting queries, the table has 40 columns and it's slow.
